title: Mid-Market Onboarding Lead
description:
What Makes Cloudbeds Unique 
 At Cloudbeds , we're not just building software, we're transforming hospitality. Our platform powers hotels across 150 countries, processing billions in bookings annually. From boutique properties to large hotel groups, we help hoteliers transform operations and uplevel their commercial strategy through a unified platform that integrates with hundreds of partners. And we do it with a completely remote team. Imagine working alongside global innovators to build AI-powered solutions that solve hoteliers' biggest challenges. Since our founding in 2012, we've continually been recognized for excellence, most recently earning top honors at the 2026 HotelTechAwards for Best Hotel Management Software and landing on Deloitte's Technology Fast 500 again, but we're just getting started.
 How You'll Make an Impact: 
 As Mid-Market Onboarding Lead for North America, you'll own the onboarding experience for our most important growth market: independent hotels, resorts, and multi-property groups moving to Cloudbeds, often from enterprise systems like Opera. You'll lead the regional team of Onboarding Project Managers and Mid-Market Coaches who take these customers from signed contract through kickoff, go-live, Hypercare, and a clean handoff to Account Management. 
 This is a player-coach role. You'll build and run the team, and you'll also stay close to the work, personally overseeing a small set of our most strategic North American accounts and stepping in when a project is at risk. Our mid-market customers expect a partner who understands their operation, not just our software. You'll set that standard: consultative kickoffs, clear expectations, and guidance on how their workflows and SOPs should change, not only which buttons to click. 
 You'll report to the Global Director of Mid-Market Onboarding and work alongside regional leads in LATAM, EMEA, and APAC. You'll be measured on time-to-live, deployment quality, onboarding CSAT, early-lifecycle retention, and the strength and readiness of your team. 
 Our Mid-Market Onboarding Team: 
 Our Mid-Market Onboarding team is a global group of former hoteliers, project managers, and implementation specialists. We're purpose-built for complex customers: coaches carry fewer accounts so they can go deeper, every project has structure, and the first days after go-live are covered by a dedicated Hypercare phase. We test and learn constantly, use AI and automation to strip out admin work, and save our time for what matters most: building trust and helping hoteliers run a better operation from day one. Our principle: standardize the repeatable, personalize the meaningful.

 Lead, coach, and develop the North America team of Onboarding Project Managers and Mid-Market Coaches, including team members based in Latin America who serve North American customers, with clear expectations, regular 1:1s, performance management, and growth paths 
 Raise the bar on customer-facing quality: run call reviews and kickoff prep, and coach the team on tone, how to frame product limitations, and when and how to have hard conversations, so that kickoffs build confidence instead of creating escalations 
 Personally oversee a small portfolio of strategic North American key accounts and multi-property groups, serving as their senior onboarding contact and staying involved through go-live and handoff 
 Own account intake and assignment for the region: review key-account and exception requests, match each account to the right OPM or coach based on complexity and capacity, and keep workloads within target 
 Act as the first escalation point for at-risk North American onboardings. Diagnose what went wrong, reset the plan with the customer, and decide when to bring in Professional Services, certified consultant partners, or a different owner 
 Ramp new hires quickly: run regional training and shadowing, certify readiness before new team members take live accounts, and help shape hiring profiles as the team grows 
 Track and improve regional performance on time-to-live, deployment quality, onboarding CSAT, Hypercare outcomes, and early retention, using Salesforce dashboards and onboarding tooling to spot risk early

 Coordinate with third-party consultants and partners who lead or support implementations for some of our customers 
 Take on the day-to-day leadership load (team questions, case investigations, call coverage) so the team keeps moving and senior leadership can focus on strategy 
 Use AI and automation to cut administrative work for yourself and your team

 5+ years in hotel operations or hospitality technology (a hotel, hotel group or management company, or a PMS/hospitality software company). Experience limited to OTAs, GDS, or travel distribution does not meet this requirement 
 2+ years directly managing customer-facing team members in onboarding, implementation, professional services, or customer success, including hiring, coaching, and performance management

 Strong understanding of North American hotel operations: front office, reservations, distribution, revenue management, payments, and reporting

title: Regional Revenue Operations Manager
description:
At SiteMinder, we believe our success comes from our people. We build diverse, inclusive teams where different voices, backgrounds and perspectives are valued. Our differences drive innovation for our customers, and our people bring the ideas, expertise and energy that help us keep moving forward. We’re better together.

What We Do...

Right now, somewhere in the world, a hotel is taking a booking or increasing their revenue through technology you could help build. SiteMinder is the world’s leading hotel commerce platform. For more than 20 years, we’ve helped hotels attract guests, maximise revenue, forecast demand and perform at their best. Today, our platform supports 56,000+ hotels in 150+ countries, connects to 3,000+ partners and powers more than 140m reservations and AU$85 billion+ in hotel revenue each year.

That’s the kind of impact your work can have here. You’ll solve meaningful challenges with AI, simplify complexity and build solutions that help hotels perform. Supported by clear purpose, a strong platform and teams who care about what they’re building, you’ll have the opportunity to shape the future of an industry that never stands still.

About the Regional Revenue Operations Manager role...

We are looking for a strategic Revenue Operations professional to help align and optimise our go-to-market teams.

In this role, you’ll play a key role in unifying go-to-market teams, aligning goals, and helping the organisation achieve sustainable revenue growth.

You will leverage data-driven insights to enhance operational efficiency, streamline processes, and on supporting and optimising the sales processes within a specific geographic region, ensuring alignment with company-wide sales goals and providing actionable insights to drive performance. 

The role often involves working closely with regional sales teams, sales leaders, and cross-functional departments such as marketing, finance, and customer success.

 

What you’ll do…

 - Regional Strategy Development: Collaborate with regional management to design and execute revenue strategies that align with company goals and priorities.

 - Data Analysis and Reporting: Break down regional performance metrics to identify trends, opportunities, and gaps; prepare reports and presentations for senior management.

 - Performance Tracking and Forecasting: Monitor and evaluate key performance indicators (KPIs), and contribute to accurate revenue forecasting and planning processes.

 - Technology Oversight: Manage and optimise the use of sales and marketing technologies (CRM other tools) to support revenue operations.

 - Local Market Insights: Gather and break down market intelligence to inform strategic decisions and adapt strategies to meet regional needs.
   
    

What you have…

 - Extensive experience in revenue operations, sales operations, or related roles, with a focus on regional management.

 - Proficiency in data analysis and reporting tools.

 - Advanced Microsoft Excel / Google Sheets experience is essential. SQL is desirable.

 - Familiarity with Salesforce and other sales/marketing technologies.

 

Our Perks & Benefits…

- Equity packages for you to be a part of the SiteMinder journey 

- Hybrid working model (in-office & from home)

- Mental health and well-being initiatives

- Generous parental (including secondary) leave policy

- Paid birthday, study and volunteering leave every year

- Sponsored social clubs, team events, and celebrations

- Employee Resource Groups (ERG) to help you connect and get involved 

- Investment in your personal growth offering training for your advancement

Think this role sounds like you? If so, we’d love to hear from you. Please send us your resume and our Talent Acquisition team will be in touch.

 

When you apply, feel free to share your pronouns and let us know if you need any adjustments during the interview process, we’re here to support you. We also warmly encourage applications from people from underrepresented backgrounds.

title: Connectivity Partner Manager
description:
Airbnb was born in 2007 when two hosts welcomed three guests to their San Francisco home, and has since grown to over 5 million hosts who have welcomed over 2 billion guest arrivals in almost every country across the globe. Every day, hosts offer unique stays and experiences that make it possible for guests to connect with communities in a more authentic way. 
 The Community You Will Join:  
 The Airbnb Hotels team is a fun, fast-growing group leading Airbnb’s expansion into the hotel sector. Operating with an entrepreneurial spirit, this team combines the simplicity, product excellence, and guest-centered ethos that define Airbnb. This team’s mission is to deliver the smoothest, most intuitive hotel booking experience for guests, while helping hotels easily drive incremental bookings so they can focus on delivering the best hospitality. The ultimate aim is to help more people discover high-quality hotels, creating value for guests and our hotel partners. 
 The Difference You Will Make: 
 We’re looking for an experienced Connectivity Partner Manager to own the health and growth of our network of connectivity providers, including channel managers, property management systems (PMS), central reservation systems (CRS) and other integration partners. You’ll join the Global Hotels Connectivity team, which owns Airbnb’s global relationships with hotel connectivity providers. Using data, automation, and scaled programs, you’ll keep your portfolio integrated and compliant, improving connection quality and operations in close partnership with internal stakeholders.
 The ideal candidate is a technical expert with strong project management experience, analytical acumen, and excellent communication skills.
 A Typical Day:  
 Own end-to-end connection performance across a network of connectivity partners, delivering day-to-day support through scaled programs.
 Build deep knowledge of technical integrations across PMS, CRS and Channel Managers, to provide targeted partner support.
 Use data to identify strategic opportunities and drive growth.
 Own scaled communications to all partners on feature updates, mandatory API changes, and deprecations, with clear timelines and next steps.
 Educate partners on product updates and share partner feedback with internal stakeholders.
 Troubleshoot partner technical issues to ensure performance.
 Develop and maintain technical partner resources that support field teams to self-serve.
 Represent Airbnb at external meetings and industry events, engaging with connectivity and hotel partners.
 Work with your team to design and manage projects that support the commercial goals of Airbnb and our hotel and connectivity partners.

 6+ years of experience in a Connectivity Partner Manager or Technical Partner Manager role within a global technology or hospitality tech company.
 Strong understanding of hospitality/travel software; PMS, CRS, Channel Managers.
 Proficiency in SQL, Looker and Excel. 
 Tableau, Asana, Jira  and Salesforce experience preferred.
 Solid technical troubleshooting skills and project management experience.
 Excellent communication and presentation abilities, with confidence in engaging clients across multiple channels with stakeholders at various levels. 
 Effective time management and ability to prioritize in a fast-paced environment.
 Strong quantitative skills with a proven ability to leverage data in decision-making.
 Adaptability to shifting priorities, projects, and deadlines.
 Passion for Airbnb, travel, and the sharing economy—being an Airbnb host is a plus

title: Team Lead, Onboarding Operations
description:
At Playlist, life's richest moments happen when people step away from screens to move, connect, explore, and play. We're building the definitive platform for intentional living, connecting people with inspiring experiences in fitness, wellness, and beyond. With popular brands like Mindbody and ClassPass, Playlist empowers businesses and individuals, making it effortless for aspirations to become actions. Join us in reshaping technology's role to foster meaningful, real-world connections.
 Mindbody equips wellness entrepreneurs with technology to support thriving businesses and create exceptional experiences. Innovation and curiosity drive our culture, connecting businesses and individuals through cutting-edge solutions. Join us if you're passionate about enhancing wellness through technology.
 The role you'll play
 This role oversees the full launch and onboarding for all ClassPass business verticals including fitness, wellness and food and beverage. The team is responsible for the onboarding experience of our partners.
 You deliver against and contribute the team's operating plan, represent Onboarding in the cross-functional forums where Sales, Product, and Operations make decisions about it, and are accountable for the numbers as the Team Lead for Onboarding, you own this team end to end. You partner with the outsourced delivery team's team leads on day-to-day priorities and performance, lead a small internal team of a quality and an enablement specialist, and are the first internal point of contact when a launch is at risk. You support the Manager, Business Operations on larger strategic initiatives and bring data-backed recommendations from the floor. You manage how fast partners launch, how many stall or get sent back, and the quality of what goes live.
 You set a high standard and hold the team to it, you build the routines and operating cadences that keep it delivering without you in the room, and you identify and drive improvements to how the team works.
 What you'll do
 Team goals and cross-functional partnership 
 Track, report and contribute to Onboarding's goals and scorecard in weekly business reviews
 Represent Onboarding in cross-functional forums with Sales, Product, and Operations, and follow through on decisions and owners
 Contribute to the plan for reducing delayed and returned launches and execute the team's part of it
 Bring data-backed recommendations on what to automate or improve to the Manager, Business Operations
 Vendor performance 
 Track vendor performance against SLAs and scorecards, prepare inputs for business reviews, and escalate performance concerns to the Manager, Business Operations
 Work with the vendor's team leads day to day to set priorities, review performance, and agree on corrective action when metrics slip
 Lead as a player-coach: regularly review calls, cases, and templates yourself to find where the team can get better, and turn what you find into coaching, process changes, and training

 Own time-to-launch, the launch backlog, onboarding speed, and quality and error rates, and act on them daily
 Maintain clear ownership and visibility across the launch queue so at-risk and aging launches are caught and worked early
 Capacity planning 
 Forecast demand against actual headcount and schedule adherence for the outsourced team using workforce management tools such as Assembled, and adjust staffing and coverage with the vendor ahead of volume changes
 Process, quality, and enablement 
 Own the onboarding playbooks and SOPs and keep them current as the product and the partner mix change
 Run QA calibration with your quality specialist and the vendor so scoring is consistent and coaching is targeted
 Own the training content the vendor delivers, through your enablement specialist, so agents are always working from current material
 Partner escalations 
 Act as the first internal escalation point when a launch is at risk, resolve what's in scope, escalate what isn't, and feed what you learn back into process and training
 People leadership 
 Lead, coach, and develop a small team, a quality specialist and an enablement specialist: set clear expectations, give regular feedback, and manage performance

 Onboarding experience across more than one vertical, such as fitness, food and beverage, wellness, or experiences

description:
ABOUT RAMP

Ramp is building the smart infrastructure for finance teams, embedded in the transaction flow of every dollar a business spends. We automate how over $275B in annualized spend flows in and out of 85,000+ companies: authorizing payments, flagging risk, categorizing spend, and closing books.

The problems are high-stakes, data-dense, and unforgiving.

We hire people with high agency and high urgency. We look for slope over intercept. We care less about where you trained and more about what you’ve built. At Ramp, everyone is a builder who owns problems end to end and makes consequential decisions that shape the outcome.

The median Ramp customer saves 7.5% and grows revenue 16% in their first year – far in excess of businesses operating without Ramp. We believe every ambitious company deserves the same.

If you want to build systems that directly shape how companies move and manage billions, Ramp is the place to do it.




ABOUT THE ROLE

Ramp builds software that moves real money, from bill payments and corporate cards to reimbursements, accounting integrations, and travel. Our customers rely on us to keep their operations running: invoices get paid, books get closed, and finance leaders can trust the data behind every decision.

In this role, you will be the person who spots where customers are getting stuck and drives issues to a clear resolution. You will learn a complex product deeply enough to troubleshoot across payments, bank linking, accounting syncs, and card programs, then partner with teams across Engineering, Risk, Product, and Partnerships to get problems solved. This is not script-based support. You will triage, investigate, and make high-signal judgment calls throughout the day.

You will thrive in this role if you are a systems thinker and deeply customer obsessed. Support is the baseline. How you think about improving processes, tools, and outcomes is what sets you apart.

 


WHAT YOU’LL DO

 - Be the voice of Ramp's Customer Support. You'll spend your day engaging with customers, primarily via live calls, email, and chat.

 - Diagnose across a broad product surface. Ramp isn't one product — it's payments, cards, travel, accounting integrations, and more. You'll need to understand how they connect and where they break.

 - Operate with an ownership mindset, managing escalations end-to-end. You take full accountability for every ticket you handle. When an issue crosses team boundaries — risk, engineering, product, partnerships — you route it correctly, follow up, and make sure the customer isn't left waiting. You'll work across Zendesk, internal tooling, and Slack-based escalation workflows.

 - Build and shape AI tools, not just use them. Ramp is building AI into CX operations. You'll use AI-powered research tools and proprietary tools like Glass daily, provide direct feedback on what's working, and play an active role in how these tools evolve. You're not just a user — you're a builder. We are all builders at Ramp.

 - Ship improvements, not just flag them. When you notice a process gap, a missing SOP, or a knowledge base article that's sending associates down the wrong path, you don't just raise it — you have the autonomy to roll up your sleeves and fix it. Leverage AI to solve problems, build automations, and improve the systems around you. The best people in this role make the whole team better.

 - Communicate with precision and empathy. Our customers are financially sophisticated. You need to explain what's happening, what you're doing about it, and what they should expect — clearly and without filler.


WHAT YOU NEED

 - You're a systems thinker: you don't just solve the ticket in front of you, you ask why the problem exists and how to prevent it from happening again.

 - You actively use AI tools — Claude, Notion AI, research and workflow tools — and can demonstrate how you've applied them to get real work done. This is a hard requirement.

 - You're fast-moving while holding yourself to a high bar for execution: you balance speed, accuracy, and thoroughness in every interaction.

 - You can hold a technical conversation about how systems connect (APIs, bank integrations, accounting software) even if you're not writing code.

 - You manage competing priorities without dropping things. When you have 15 open issues across 4 internal teams, nothing falls through.

 - You write clearly and concisely. You can explain a payment reconciliation issue to a CFO without jargon.

 - You're comfortable on the phone. Many interactions start there.

 - You have a demonstrated track record of exceeding key performance standards, including CSAT, QA, and speed-of-service metrics.


NICE TO HAVES

 - Experience building workflows or automations using AI tools, not just prompting

 - Familiarity with accounting workflows (AP/AR, GL, reconciliation) or ERP integrations (NetSuite, QuickBooks, Sage)

 - Background in payments infrastructure (ACH, wire transfers, card networks)

 - Track record of working somewhere that shipped product fast and expected CX to keep up


WHY BE A CX ASSOCIATE AT RAMP

 - Cross-functional exposure from day one. You work directly with Product, Engineering, and GTM teams — not siloed into a support queue.

 - AI tools and unlimited access. Unlimited tokens, proprietary AI tools like Glass, and a culture that expects you to use them to move faster and build smarter.

 - Career growth that you own. Grow within CX, explore other functions internally, or carve out a path that doesn't exist yet. If you're invested, we're invested.

 - Culture that's different from a call center. Team events, in-person offsites, and a genuine commitment to building a team people want to be part of.

 About the role 
 Let's get into the specifics. It’s impossible to capture every nuance of a role – especially at a rapidly growing company like Mews – but if we had to distil it into a job description (which we do because this is a job description), it would be this:
 You'd own one Mews product area end to end from the Specialist Hub: the hardest technical implementations in it, the escalations that Onboarding Managers and Support can't resolve from the knowledge base, and the operational health of the whole thing, from onboarding performance and SLAs to the documentation the rest of Customer Success relies on. You sit between Onboarding, Customer Success, Product and R&D, with a direct line into testing, blitz testing and product feedback, so what you learn from customers shapes what gets built.

 Support complex implementations for your product area, including configuration, integrations, APIs and non-standard requirements, and act as the technical escalation point when something is blocking a go-live

 AI Fluency Level 3 or the equivalent hands-on experience: you've already redesigned how you or your team works using AI, and you check what it produces rather than taking it at face value

 Working knowledge of Salesforce, Jira and Confluence

 A bachelor's degree in a relevant field, or equivalent practical experience

Through our unparalleled science, data, technology and laboratory network, we advance diagnostics, accelerate innovation and help address some of the world’s most important health challenges. Together, we’re improving health and improving lives.
 Lead IT Implementation Specialist 
 The Lead IT Implementation Specialist is responsible for leading enterprise-wide laboratory system implementations, validations, upgrades, and enhancements. This role combines clinical laboratory expertise with information technology implementation experience to support the successful deployment and adoption of laboratory software solutions across the organization.
 The individual collaborates with business and technical stakeholders to coordinate implementation activities, manage solution delivery, support operational readiness, and ensure successful transition of systems into production environments. This role applies advanced laboratory and technical knowledge to improve implementation effectiveness, drive user adoption, and support scalable technology delivery across the enterprise.
 Our ideal candidate combines hands-on clinical laboratory experience, such as Medical Laboratory Scientist (MLS), Medical Laboratory Technician (MLT), or related laboratory roles, with experience implementing, validating, supporting, or deploying laboratory information systems and technology solutions.

 Drive continuous improvement of implementation methodologies, validation processes, and deployment standards.
 Develop and maintain implementation documentation, validation records, training materials, and operational support documentation.
 Ensure effective transition of implemented solutions into operational support models.

 Launch Potato is the discovery and conversion company. We reach tens of millions of people every month through our brands, including FinanceBuzz, All About Cookies, and OnlyInYourState. We turn that attention into real outcomes for our partners, some of the world's leading companies.

The pace is real, and change is constant, so the people who do best turn change into opportunity instead of waiting for it to settle. Feedback runs direct and lands with respect. Ordinary people make themselves extraordinary at Launch Potato . 
 THE ROLE 
 We're looking for a hands-on Partnerships & BD expert to grow our banking, deposits, and investing partners, and to bring on the ones we haven't met yet.  Fluency in performance economics, including CPA, CPL, CPC, and revenue share, and the business acumen to use performance, revenue, and unit-economic data in a negotiation.
 Strong communication, relationship building, and negotiation across several partners and opportunities at once.
 NICE TO HAVE 
 Publisher experience, or enough of the language to hold the conversation.
 Experience in wealth management, financial advisory, RIAs, or advisor networks.
 Existing relationships with banks, fintech companies, investment platforms, or related financial-services companies.
 Experience selling customer acquisition, media, lead generation, or performance-based marketing.
